convoLines.text: "Tell you what — Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Tariq. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Tariq. Nobody's settled it."
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
Counted.
"Still on that favor."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big-Bane' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Karen?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my mother, Karen. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half. She made soup from nothing and they called that boring. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming.
Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Anyway, that's me."
"I dreamed Robin was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sleep's gone strange. I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The System's like weather. You don't argue with weather. You build a roof."
"We started on what's been happening, then got onto the big questions."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About this wound — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Robin died... I keep expecting to see Robin at the fire. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway — I should get going."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Kwame sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Kwame shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. You know?"
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Doesn't matter now."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Dineo is gone and Somchai is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Гей... ти розмовляєш українською? Ні? ...бляха.»
«Правильно.» They nod back, slowly. "Food?"
«Все буде добре.» (you catch 'добре' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Я цього тобі ніколи не забуду.» (you catch 'забуду' — forget) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about that favor — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Right. Action time. You know where to find me.'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"As I said — Still on that favor."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
The tension eases back to something ordinary.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Dineo is gone and Somchai is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I retie every loose knot in passing. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Robin Schulz is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Robin Schulz is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d10: ◈ CRISIS — THE FIRST GRAVE. Dante is dead. The village digs its first grave, and everyone understands at once: this place can kill you. It just did.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Robin home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d10: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d10: SYSTEM: "Oh. Oh no. Was that supposed to happen? The audience is crying. I did not know they could do that."
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d10: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d11: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 35. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d11: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d11: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.

d11: That night, they bring Robin home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d13: You say a few words for Robin. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d13: You bury Robin. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d13: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
